podcast.title: Rotating Stage Uniforms and Surgical Masks
podcast.body: Hailing from Liverpool, Clinic employs a unique visual strategy by rotating five different stage uniforms. A consistent and striking element of their performances is that the band members always wear surgical masks, contributing to their enigmatic and distinctive stage presence. "And also from Liverpool, there's clinic. They rotate five different stage uniforms, and they always perform wearing surgical masks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: House Looting Post-Rehab (1995)
xref.body: After a period at a rehabilitation clinic in the Arizona desert, Dave Gahan was released on August 27, 1995. Upon returning to his house, he discovered it had been completely looted and burglarized. This incident immediately prompted him to use heroin ("smack") and check into the Sunset Marquis hotel. "But when he checked out on August 27, 1995 and returned to his house, he found that it had been completely looted, burgl'd."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Liver Transplant at Cleveland Clinic (2013)
xref.body: In May 2013, Lou Reed traveled to the Cleveland Clinic to undergo a liver transplant, receiving a donor liver that a doctor described as "less than perfect" but still preferable given his critical condition. "In May 2013, he flew to the Cleveland Clinic where he had a liver transplant."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Career Transition to Chiropractic
xref.body: After numerous gigs with various bands, Terry Chimes retired from music by 1994 to pursue his passion for biology, medicine, and healing. He opened a chiropractic clinic in Essex, which later expanded into a chain of clinics, and he began giving lectures on alternative medicine. "by 1994, he'd retired from music and opened a chiropractic clinic in Essex."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Chiropractic Clinic in Essex
xref.body: Today, Terry Chimes runs his own chiropractic clinic located in Essex. "And today, Terry Chimes has a chiropractic clinic in Essex."

xref.title: Involvement with Innocence Project
xref.body: Brian "Dexter" Holland actively works with the Innocence Project, a non-profit legal clinic. This organization offers DNA testing to individuals convicted of crimes, helping them prove their innocence through scientific evidence. "Dexter works with a charity called Innocence Project, which is a non-profit legal clinic that offers DNA testing for people convicted of crimes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Liver Rejection and Final Decline
xref.body: Following an initial period of improvement, Lou Reed's body began to reject the new liver, causing his skin to turn yellow and him to lose weight again, leading doctors at the Cleveland Clinic to inform him that he had run out of options. "But then things started to fail again. His body began to reject the new liver."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Steve Guthrie's Healthcare Career
xref.body: Steve Guthrie, a former member of the goth band Theater of Hate, is now a practicing acupuncturist in Brighton. He serves as the director of the Dijkrode Natural Health Clinic and has also contributed to establishing a non-profit health clinic for children. "Steve Guthrie was a member of a Gothband called Theater of Hate."
